key_insight: Matlantis PFP v9 expands r2SCAN-based training coverage to 96 elements and additional domains, including clusters and adsorption structures.
engineering_relevance: The expanded potential enables larger-scale atomistic simulations involving rare-earth and actinide elements, as well as molecular adsorption on surfaces.
method: Extend r2SCAN training data to lanthanides Pr–Lu and elements Po–Cm.
Add cluster and adsorption configurations to broaden domain coverage.
Evaluate crystal formation energies, adsorption energies, and A100 GPU performance.
evidence_signal: New-element crystal formation energies retain comparable experimental agreement to previously supported compositions; on A100 GPUs, force evaluation is 3–4× faster and maximum atom counts are 5–10× larger than SevenNet-Omni.
watch_item: Chemisorbed species are overbound despite overall adsorption-energy errors comparable to DFT-PBE against experiment.
paper_title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
